description: Take the Potala Palace apart piece by piece in 3D, and read the story of the Dalai Lamas' winter palace: thirteen stories on Red Hill, a thousand rooms, eight golden tombs, and the film that recreated it in Argentina.

hotspots.text: The Red Palace (Potrang Marpo), added 1690-1694, is the religious heart of the complex: chapels, shrines, libraries of Buddhist scripture and the assembly hall, all behind crimson battered walls.
hotspots.title: The Red Palace

hotspots.text: One of eight golden stupas, the tombs of eight Dalai Lamas, sheathed in gold inside the Red Palace. They are the spiritual and material center of the building.
hotspots.title: The golden stupas

hotspots.text: The White Palace (Potrang Karpo), completed 1648-1649, was the secular machine: living quarters, offices, the seminary and the printing house. Its whitewashed walls slope inward in the Tibetan manner.
hotspots.title: The White Palace

hotspots.text: The top-floor Chambers of Sunshine let in daylight all day at 3,700 meters; the Dalai Lama wintered here. Old rules admitted only monks above the fourth rank to the western chamber.
hotspots.title: Chambers of Sunshine

hotspots.text: The monks' great assembly hall, its carved and painted columns holding up a room built for ritual. The palace murals alone cover some 2,500 square meters.
hotspots.title: The assembly hall

hotspots.text: The long southern stair climbs Marpo Ri to the palace gates. Pilgrims still circle the hill on the Lingkhor path below.
hotspots.title: The grand stair

intro: Thirteen stories on a red hill at 3,700 meters, with walls five meters thick at the base and copper poured into the foundations against earthquakes. This is the Potala Palace: a thousand rooms, eight golden tombs, and the most famous Tibetan building in the world.
page_title: Potala Palace: Exploded 3D Model and History | Architectural Atlas

sections.body:
The hill was sacred before it was a palace. King Songtsen Gampo meditated in a cave on Marpo Ri and built the first palace there in 637, traditionally to greet his bride, Princess Wencheng of the Tang Dynasty. That building stood for a thousand years.

In 1645 Lozang Gyatso, the Great Fifth Dalai Lama, ordered the present palace on the same summit, advised that the site between Drepung and Sera monasteries and the old city was ideal as a seat of government. The White Palace was finished by 1648-1649: the Dalai Lamas' residence and the offices of Tibetan rule. The Red Palace followed in 1690-1694, built by more than 7,000 workers and 1,500 artists and craftsmen, to house the religion the palace served.
sections.heading: A thousand years on Red Hill

sections.body:
The numbers are the architecture. The complex measures 400 meters east to west and 350 north to south. Its sloping stone walls average 3 meters thick, 5 meters at the base, with molten copper poured into the foundations as earthquake protection. Thirteen stories rise about 117 meters above the hilltop, holding more than 1,000 rooms, 10,000 shrines and some 200,000 statues.

The division is functional and chromatic. The White Palace is secular: the Eastern Hall where Dalai Lamas were enthroned, the Chambers of Sunshine, the seminary, the printing house. The Red Palace is sacred: the eight golden stupas, the chapels, the libraries. Five roofs are sheathed in gilded bronze. Every hall has a skylight for the thin high-altitude daylight, and the corridors are deliberately narrow against the spacious halls, solemnity built into the plan.
sections.heading: Two palaces, one mountain

sections.body:
In March 1959 the 14th Dalai Lama fled Lhasa for India, and the palace that had been his winter residence became a museum. Unlike most Tibetan religious structures, it was not sacked in the years that followed, and its chapels and artifacts survive remarkably intact.

In 1997 Hollywood told the palace's story without ever filming there. Jean-Jacques Annaud's Seven Years in Tibet, about Heinrich Harrer's years with the young 14th Dalai Lama, was shot principally in Argentina, in the foothills of the Andes around Uspallata, with additional work in Canada, Austria and Britain. Annaud later confirmed that two crews secretly filmed about twenty minutes of material in Tibet itself. Brad Pitt, David Thewlis and Annaud were barred from entering China, and the film was never shown there.

The palace's other great appearance needs no camera. The Potala stands on the back of the 50-yuan note of the fifth series of the renminbi; two senior artists of the China Banknote Printing and Minting Corporation traveled to Lhasa to research the engraving. It is one of the few buildings in the world you can spend.

timeline.text: Songtsen Gampo builds the first palace on Marpo Ri.
The 5th Dalai Lama orders the present palace; the White Palace (Potrang Karpo) is completed 1648-1649.
The Red Palace (Potrang Marpo) is added by 7,000 workers and 1,500 artists.
The 13th Dalai Lama renovates chapels and adds two stories to the Red Palace.
The 14th Dalai Lama flees to India; the palace becomes a museum.
Seven Years in Tibet recreates Lhasa in Argentina; the production is barred from China.
